solutionSql:
SELECT c.id AS customer_id, c.name AS customer_name,
       COUNT(s.id) FILTER (WHERE i.id IS NULL)::integer AS unbilled_shipments
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN shipments s ON s.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.shipment_id = s.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.id;

rules.howSolved: Kept customers as the driving table with LEFT JOINs to shipments and invoices, so every customer row survives.
COUNT(s.id) counts only real shipment rows, so a customer with no shipments gets 0 instead of the placeholder count.
Kept the LEFT JOIN to invoices and counted shipments where i.id IS NULL, meaning no invoice row references the shipment.

ambiguities: The ticket says to repair the supplied query. I read its only defect as COUNT(*) counting the LEFT JOIN placeholder row, and changed it to COUNT(s.id) FILTER (WHERE i.id IS NULL). I found no other defect in the starter.
notes: The schema says there is at most one invoice per shipment; I checked this on all datasets used by the item (no shipment has more than one invoice), so the invoice join cannot multiply rows. Row counts per dataset: sample=8, nulls=8, ties=8, boundary=8. Ran on every listed dataset without error.
